decisions.statement: The record names when the shell ended.
The record names the status that shell ended with.
The record names where that shell was.
A shell is told apart from a later shell of the same pid by when the shell started.
The start is read out of the shell's own entry in the process table.
A status above a hundred and twenty-eight names the signal that ended the shell.
A hangup is recorded and then re-raised so the shell dies of the signal that reached that shell.
Only a terminal the editor opened is trapped.
A shell that could not leave a record ends as that shell would have ended anyway.
The record sits beside the pages of the page type that record describes.
A folder not there yet is made rather than the record being dropped.
The line naming the checkout is handed in rather than spelled here.

definition: how an editor terminal's shell ended, left beside that terminal's own page
